subject: Re: Renewal mechanics and termination carveouts — Greenfield MSA redlines
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@greenfield.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@greenfield.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed redlines to MSA — notice windows and termination

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team is excited about the performance benchmarks. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed the MSA and Order Form and came back with a couple of asks that are blocking internal approval:

- Auto-renew notice: we need a 120-day notice for auto-renew rather than 60. Procurement says that aligns with our procurement cycle.
- Termination for convenience: redlines propose removal of T-for-convenience entirely; they prefer explicit right to terminate without cause at the Order Form level only, not in the MSA, and with a 60-day notice.

I attached our redlines for reference. Can you confirm whether Redwood would accept (a) extending the auto-renew notice window to 120 days, and (b) either keeping T-for-convenience limited to the Order Form or removing it?

Also, please call out any commercial or implementation impacts for our procurement and finance teams. We are on a tight timebox — procurement hopes to finish review by 12/07 so we can hit our year-end internal approval.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Head of Procurement
Greenfield Analytics
[Attachment: greenfield_redlines_MSA.pdf (pdf)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:01:00 -08:00

Team — forwarding incoming redlines from Greenfield (attached). High level asks: 120-day auto-renew notice; removal/relocation of termination-for-convenience. Procurement needs an answer by 12/07.

Quick context: Greenfield is a mid-market analytics customer; deal size ~ $320k ARR, Dedicated plan, target go-live Jan. Negotiation leash is moderate — revenue is helpful but we need to protect predictability for capacity planning. 

Requesting legal position + a recommended concession we can propose that balances commercial risk and procurement ask. Short bullets would be great.

Thanks — I'll stay looped for any final language we send.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 14:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed redlines to MSA — notice windows and termination

Vanessa / Laura — reviewed Greenfield's redlines. My suggested compromise:

1) Auto-renew notice window: counter with 60 days in the MSA (our standard) BUT offer a 120-day notice as an Order Form-level commercial concession for this specific deal. Rationale: keeps our master MSA intact while satisfying procurement by making it a deal-specific term.

2) Termination for convenience: do NOT remove from the MSA. Instead:
   - Keep a narrow T-for-convenience in the MSA limited to termination by either party with 90 days' written notice but capped damages (e.g., termination fee equal to 3 months of committed spend or unused pre-paid credits).
   - Alternatively, allow Customer to have T-for-convenience only in the Order Form for the initial 12-month term with 60-day notice if Redwood keeps MSA-level language that prohibits wholesale removal.

3) Implementation/commercial impact: 120-day notice at Order Form level could delay our ability to reallocate dedicated capacity but is manageable given the deal size. A capped termination fee protects against churn-related revenue loss and resource churn.

I attached a short markup of the Order Form with a proposed 120-day clause and a sample termination fee line. If Sales is comfortable, we should send this as a written offer and ask procurement to confirm acceptance by 12/07.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_proposed_orderform_markup.docx (docx)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed redlines to MSA — notice windows and termination

Agree with Karthik's recommendation. A couple of operational asks before we send:

- Finance: please confirm the proposed termination fee (3 months committed spend) is acceptable to revenue recognition and that we can invoice that on termination.
- Sales ops / onboarding: if we put a 120-day Order Form notice, we need to document expected deprovisioning timeline for Dedicated pool capacity so CS knows the handoff.

Vanessa — go ahead and share Karthik's markup with Greenfield as a written compromise. Ask them to confirm by 12/07 and include procurement/finance in the reply so we have a single thread. If they push to remove MSA-level T-for-convenience, escalate to me immediately.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@greenfield.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines to MSA — notice windows and termination

Marta — thank you for the redlines and the quick turnaround. We reviewed with legal and ops and can offer the following compromise to get you through procurement approval: 

- Auto-renew notice: Redwood's standard MSA remains 60 days, but we will include a deal-specific Order Form provision granting Greenfield a 120-day notice for the initial term of this Order Form only (will be explicit in the Order Form).

- Termination for convenience: We cannot remove T-for-convenience from the MSA, but we're prepared to:
  * Narrow the MSA's T-for-convenience (mutual right) to require 90 days' written notice and a capped termination fee equal to 3 months of committed spend, OR
  * If Greenfield prefers, we can limit the right to terminate for convenience to the Order Form for the initial 12-month term with 60 days' notice (this would create a deal-level right and leave the MSA intact).

Please let us know which option you prefer by COB 12/07 so we can finalize and circulate an executed Order Form. We've copied our counsel (Karthik) and ops lead (Laura) for any follow-up on invoicing and deprovisioning timelines. 

Attached: Redwood's proposed Order Form markup that implements the 120-day notice and the termination fee language.

If this sounds acceptable I'll prepare a clean Order Form and send for signature via DocuSign.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
